summary: Sagar Uday More works in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He earned an MBBS and DNB at Niga Hospital and became a member of the Epigraphical Society of India in 2025.
Working in computational studies and Indology, Sai Susarla served as Dean at MIT World Peace University (attested 2019) and held a post at the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation (attested 2025).

Sai Venkatesh Balasubramanian works in Indology and computational fields. He earned a B.Tech (2007-2011) and Ph.D. (2014) from SASTRA, an MBA from Assam Don Bosco University (2012-2014), and worked at IBM India (2011-2012).

Said Reza Huseini is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at King's College London, Jawaharlal Nehru University (MPhil 2014-2015), Leiden University (BA 2015-2024), and the University of Cambridge (MA 2021-2025).

Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi (1921-1994) worked in Indology and history. He studied at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University and under Mohammad Habib, later holding posts at Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, and Australian National University (Reader, 1967-1986).

Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Peter Harvey and Max Deeg, completing an MPhil at Cardiff University (2014). He is attested as a PhD researcher at Ghent University in 2026.

Sakunoshin Motoda (1862-1928) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kenyon College (~1888-1891), the University of Pennsylvania (~1891-1895), and Columbia University. He held a post at Rikkyo University (~1899-1921).

Sakutaro Fujioka (1870-1910) specialized in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1894 to 1897 and subsequently held a post there from around 1902 to 1910.

Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga (b. 1945) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and numerous traditional masters, served as Abbot of Sakya Monastery until 2017, and founded Sakya Centre, Sakya College, and Sakya Institute.

Sakyong Mipham (b. 1962) is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology figure. He studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, whom he succeeded, and was a board member at Naropa University until 2018.

Sallie B. King (b. 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz and served as Professor and Professor Emerita of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1991-2016).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman works in Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD in 1979 at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri, and became Senior Lecturer Emerita at Berkeley.

Sally McAra works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999-2000) under Christine Dureau and Karen Nero, and served there as an Honorary Research Fellow in 2019.

Sally Mellick Cutler is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She received her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford in 1993 and served as the manager of the Pali Text Society Office (attested 1996-1997).

Salome Zajadacz-Hastenrath (1932-1998) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She studied at Pädagogische Akademie Aachen (1951-1953), the University of Bonn (1956), and completed her PhD at the University of Cologne (1956-1965).

Salomon Lefmann (1831-1912) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp in Berlin (PhD ~1861-1864), Münster, Paris, and Heidelberg. From 1866, he held posts at Heidelberg University, becoming associate professor in 1870 and honorary professor in 1901.

Salomon Munk (1803-1867) was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religion. He studied in Berlin, Bonn, and Paris under Freytag, Schlegel, Lassen, and de Sacy, later cataloguing manuscripts at the BnF (1838-1850) and teaching Hebrew at Collège de France (1864-1867).

Salvador Bucca (1920-2005) studied classics at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore. A linguist and Indologist, he taught at the National University of Tucumán (1948-1951), National University of Cuyo, and served as Professor of Linguistics at Buenos Aires (1955-1983).

Sam van Schaik is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Manchester (~1996-2000). He held posts at SOAS and the British Library, where he became Head of the Endangered Archives Programme in 1999.

Samani Pratibha Pragya is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (2011-2017) and later served there as a research assistant (attested 2020).
